text:
Mira Patel: Quick follow-up on the continuous-batching RFC — two unresolved things we promised to settle: queue decomposition semantics and the kernel-handoff model. Can we decide next steps?
Alex Chen: I think the decomposition question is the bigger risk for rollout. Do we keep per-tenant micro-queues + shared coalesce, or go full shared lanes with tenant tags?
Samir Gupta: Per-tenant micro-queues gave us isolation in sims, but we saw headroom underutilization at 80% load. Shared lanes win for utilization but harder to bound tail.
Priya Rao: Re: kernel handoff — do we let the runtime choose kernels per-batch (shape-aware) or precompile a small set of kernel variants and assign at admission time? Tradeoffs: compile overhead vs suboptimal kernels.
Jon Wells: Runtime selection seems ideal for perf but adds jitter on first-seen shapes. Precompile reduces jitter but increases binary size. Also, scheduling has to be kernel-aware to avoid cross-interference.
Mira Patel: Agreed. We need a plan with experiments and a safe fallback for canary. Proposal: start with shared lanes but enforce soft headroom per-tenant, plus a tiny precompiled kernel set for common shapes, then enable runtime selection as an opt-in flag for canary tenants.
Alex Chen: Sounds reasonable. For shared lanes we'll need an enforcement primitive: soft_reservation(token_budget) that gives a tenant headroom credit but can be borrowed. Implementation: keep per-tenant credit ledger and decay policy.
Samir Gupta: Also add a fast-path admission check: if batch_shape in precompiled_set, route to precompiled kernel; else route to runtime-selection pool (slow path). That keeps p95 predictable.
Priya Rao: We should measure 3 metrics in early experiments: p99 tail latency, tail-to-median ratio, and cross-tenant fairness (median throughput deviation > 10% flags).
Jon Wells: Telemetry flags: continuous_batching.decomposition=shared-lanes, continuous_batching.kernels=hybrid. Enable a per-host flag to force precompiled-only for stress tests.
infra-bot: Deploy plan created: canary cluster "cb-v2-canary". Use config toggle: continuous_batching.v2=true. See https://go/redwood/deploys/CB-V2-Canary
Mira Patel: Thanks infra-bot. For canary tenants, we should route a small subset (5%) of traffic to cb-v2 and keep rollout throttled by observed p99 and fairness metrics.
Alex Chen: FYI - I'll add an admission metric: "enqueue_headroom_borrow_rate" to detect oscillation when shared lanes overcommit. If borrow_rate > 0.2 for sustained 2m, we auto-dampen coalesce window.
Samir Gupta: Implementation note: coalesce window damping => reduce max_coalesce_ms from 8 -> 3 for affected hosts. Need a safe cooldown and hysteresis to avoid flapping.
Priya Rao: Suggest cooldown 30s with backoff multiplier x2. Also add an override for emergency: /ops cb-evict-tenant <tenant> to force immediate per-tenant micro-queue drain.
Mira Patel: Action items: Alex to prototype credit ledger and borrow metric (ETA 4d). Samir to implement precompiled kernel selector + telemetry (ETA 6d). Priya to write the canary runbook with thresholds (ETA 2d). Jon to wire the feature flag and create the canary cluster (ETA 1d).
Jon Wells: I'll also add dashboards: p95/p99, borrow_rate, kernel_miss_rate, tenant_throughput_skew. Will link the dashboard to the runbook.
Samir Gupta: Quick question: is eviction policy normative? Do we prefer soft draining (slow) or immediate eviction if tenant violates SLO?
Mira Patel: Start soft: damp windows, throttle burst capacity, then gated immediate eviction only if canary p99 exceeds threshold for 3 consecutive windows. Avoid hard kills during early rollout.
Alex Chen: +1. Also add a unit test for credit ledger invariants and a chaos test where we spike a noisy tenant and assert borrow_rate triggers damping.
Priya Rao: I'll own the rollout doc. Will include rollback triggers: sustained p99 increase > 30% or fairness skew > 20% for 10m.
Mira Patel: Great. If nobody objects I'll merge this plan into the RFC follow-up PR and tag owners. :thumbsup:
Alex Chen: No objections. Tagging @Samir @Priya @Jon for visibility.
Samir Gupta: ack
Priya Rao: ack
Jon Wells: ack
infra-bot: Canary cluster cb-v2-canary scheduled for 2026-03-25 02:00 UTC.
